title: KOSPI Closes 4.39 Percent Higher as Samsung, SK Hynix Lead Chip Rebound
excerpt: The KOSPI surged more than 5% in early trading on November 10 before closing 4.39% higher at 5,239.13, as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix led a dip-buying rebound.
body:
• South Korea's KOSPI closed 220.28 points, or 4.39%, higher at 5,239.13 on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, snapping three straight sessions of sharp losses.
  • In early trading the index climbed 5.18% to 5,278.95 as of 9:24 a.m., with Samsung Electronics up 5.58% to 200,500 won and SK hynix up 8.27% to 1,230,000 won.
  • At the close, Samsung was up 4.74% at 198,000 won and SK hynix up 6.69% at 1.2 million won, tracking a 6.85% jump in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.
  • For investors: one rebound day follows a selloff driven by doubts over AI investment; Aju Press notes U.S. October CPI, due Tuesday evening in Seoul, is the next test.

South Korean stocks roared back on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, as dip buyers returned to the chipmakers that led last week's selloff. The benchmark KOSPI closed 220.28 points, or 4.39%, higher at 5,239.13, according to Nation Press, snapping three consecutive sessions of sharp losses.

The morning surge

The move was larger at the open. Aju Press reported the KOSPI climbed 5.18% to 5,278.95 as of 9:24 a.m., after opening 4.55% higher at 5,247.22 from Monday's close of 5,018.85 and briefly reaching 5,299.37. The Korea Exchange activated buy-side sidecars in both the KOSPI and KOSDAQ shortly after the open, suspending programme buy orders for five minutes. Advancers outnumbered decliners 746 to 118 in the main market at that point, Aju said.

Chipmakers led, in Seoul and overnight

Samsung Electronics jumped 5.58% to 200,500 won in early trading, reclaiming the 200,000-won level, and SK hynix — a major supplier of high-bandwidth memory used in AI processors — surged 8.27% to 1,230,000 won, Aju reported. By the close both had trimmed those gains: Samsung finished up 4.74% at 198,000 won and SK hynix up 6.69% at 1.2 million won, per Nation Press. The rebound followed Wall Street, where the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 6.85%, AMD surged 13.26%, Broadcom gained 8.78% and Micron rose 6.25%, according to Aju. Nvidia bucked the rally, falling 4.27%.

"U.S. semiconductor shares rose for the second consecutive session and the PHLX semiconductor index increased sharply, boosting South Korean stocks within the semiconductor value chain."

— Kim Seok-hwan, Mirae Asset Securities, via Nation Press

Who bought, and what else moved

Foreign investors returned to net buying at the close, purchasing a net 365.9 billion won, while institutions bought a net 489 billion won and retail investors sold a net 1.3 trillion won, Nation Press reported. Falling crude prices — after U.S. President Donald Trump indicated he was not prepared to resume military strikes against Iran — lifted airlines: Korean Air rose 11.51% to 32,450 won and Asiana Airlines 11.68% to 8,700 won. The won strengthened to 1,337.5 per dollar as of 3:30 p.m., Nation Press said.

What to watch next

Both reports frame this as bargain hunting after heavy selling driven by concerns about the sustainability of AI investment, not as a confirmed turn. Aju Press noted the U.S. October consumer price index is due Tuesday evening in Seoul, and that AI cloud provider CoreWeave's third-quarter discussion after Tuesday's U.S. close will give investors another read on demand for the computing capacity behind the semiconductor boom.
